answer: No single office can bless a forgery: the proof must survive three separate keepers. One threshold for every key: Ivory handle maker horn button mark carved within the polishing house, and the same receipt, each horn button is a measured tusk yield plus an ivory-carver signature, whoever holds the key. The ridge tells the panel who, the relic tells it how much, the raven tells it how long — and the panel trusts the third most of all. The threshold charges in days as well as coins: 8 days to cure a proof, and a farm cannot cure 280 proofs any faster.
